output.review_comment: The code is correct and all nine tests pass without being changed. The rule-1 check (keep words with a capital after the first letter) fixes the iPhone/NASA cases, and the first/last handling fixes 'For' and 'The'. But the patch adds an undocumented rule: a small word right after a word ending in ':' is capitalised. test_subtitle_after_colon needs this rule, and it's a normal headline-style rule rather than a one-off hack. However, the title_case docstring still says small words are lowercase 'unless it is the first or the last word of text', so the code now contradicts its own documented contract (e.g. '...field: a year...' -> '...Field: A Year...'). Please update rule 2 in the docstring to include the after-colon exception, and add a PR description saying the tests needed a rule the docstring didn't mention, so the editorial team can confirm it. Optional: the comments in the code say roughly what the code already says and could be trimmed. Fine to merge once the docstring matches the code.
